sections.label: The opening
sections.line: Short, punchy, credited, and shown not to be slop
sections.para: The AI edition is for anyone getting into AI, with practical chapters like setting up the agentic email workflow. It keeps the first edition's short, punchy style, credits Claude as co-writer with the ratio of memo to word shown, meets the slop suspicion with evidence, maps every paragraph in a graph that catches repetition, and uses synthetic readers, without fixing every issue.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Seven rules for the AI edition
sections.para: A book for anyone getting into AI; short and punchy, as readers liked the first; co-written with Claude and credited, with the ratio shown; the suspicion of slop met with evidence; every paragraph's evidence, facts, hypotheses and purpose in a graph that shows repetition; refactoring until sign-off; synthetic readers; and the right to say no.

sections.label: For anyone getting into AI
sections.line: For anyone who should get into AI
sections.para: Dinis will send this book to anyone he knows who wants or should get into AI, many without agentic workflows of their own. So one chapter should be practical: setting up a Google Workspace and the agentic workflow behind his emails, where agents draft and he sends.

sections.label: Short and punchy
sections.line: What readers liked the first time
sections.para: Readers liked the first book because it was short and punchy: despite spelling mistakes and parts that could have been expanded, it was a condensation of ideas where almost every line and paragraph made you think. The AI edition should be the same.

sections.label: Co-written with Claude
sections.line: Credit Claude, and show the ratio
sections.para: The book will be co-written with Claude and credited: Claude writes from Dinis's memos, reviews and corrections, and he reads, challenges and changes it. On this site, about 65,000 words in, 55,000 by voice, became 96,000 words of articles over four weeks, one to five words out per word in. The book will measure its own ratio and show where the voice is.

sections.label: Meet the suspicion head on
sections.para: Readers will expect AI slop, so the book should address it at the start with evidence: voice memos, quality control, editing and reviewers. Dinis's early ChatGPT deep-research pieces drew exactly that reaction; this site's articles are now called good, sometimes long, and said to sound like him. The book has to sound like that.

sections.label: Every paragraph knows what it is
sections.line: A graph that keeps the book tight
sections.para: Every paragraph, group and chapter should carry its evidence, facts, hypotheses and purpose, which makes the book a graph. A graph of graphs shows where two passages say the same thing, a common flaw in books that can no longer change. This book can be refactored right up to the end, until each part is signed off.

sections.label: Synthetic readers
sections.para: Simulated readers of different kinds will read the book and report what they understood, missed, liked and disliked, using the method already run on three sites: invented users with profiles, questions and expected paths, interviewed at the end.

sections.label: Not every issue needs raising
sections.para: Not every piece of feedback should change the book; sometimes the answer is that we are not doing it. Trying to satisfy every comment would make the book long and blunt. This site's reviews already answer every finding, with declined and a reason as a valid answer.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: What is shown and what is remembered
sections.para: The first edition's reviews are from memory, since the Amazon listing could not be read. The ratio quoted is from this site, not the book, which will measure its own. Not being slop is something to show, not claim. And synthetic readers are a tool; real readers come later.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.para: From Dinis's voice memo of 18 October 2026. Related articles cover how much of this site he wrote, how to run synthetic users, the man behind the curtain, the book's website and the plan for the AI edition.
